Daily News

Conflict · Politics

Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya minority, top UN court rules

Myanmar · Bangladesh · Major · Updated

Briefing produced 24 Nov 2026, 3:00 PM NZDT

The International Court of Justice ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya minority, marking the first time a state has been found guilty of this crime by an international court. The court determined that Myanmar had the intention to destroy a substantial part of the population, citing indiscriminate killings, sexual violence, and the destruction of evidence during 2017 clearance operations.

Why it matters

The ruling establishes a legal precedent for state responsibility under the 1948 Genocide Convention and may influence other pending ICJ cases, including one brought by South Africa against Israel. It also prompted diplomatic actions, such as the UK expelling Myanmar's defence attaché.

Daily News

Conflict · Technology · Politics

Reports: Russia may launch nuclear weapon into orbit as soon as next month

Global · Major · New

Briefing produced 24 Nov 2026, 3:00 PM NZDT

German media reported that Western intelligence agencies believe Russia may launch a nuclear-armed satellite, designated Sputnik-S, into orbit as early as December. The Kremlin dismissed the reports as unworthy of serious attention, while US officials noted that such a launch would violate the 1967 Outer Space Treaty and threaten global satellite networks.

Why it matters

A nuclear detonation in orbit would cause rapid loss of thousands of satellites and leave lingering radiation belts that could damage space assets for years, disrupting vital communications and military operations.

Daily News

AI · Science

AI claimed a solution to the 167-year-old Riemann hypothesis — and a human did, too

Global · Major · Updated

Briefing produced 24 Nov 2026, 3:00 PM NZDT

Mathematician Levent Alpöge announced a Lean-compilable solution to the Riemann hypothesis that he developed using Anthropic's Claude, while Stanford postdoc Alessandro Masullo simultaneously released a human-written proof of the General Riemann hypothesis. Independent sources have confirmed that Alpöge's formalized proof compiles successfully, though the mathematical community is still digesting the results.

Why it matters

The simultaneous release of AI-assisted and human-only proofs for a Millennium Prize problem highlights the evolving role of AI in mathematical research and the ongoing need for formal verification to validate such claims.

Daily News

Conflict · Politics

Israeli military completes ground operation in Gaza beyond Yellow Line

Gaza · Major · Catch up

Briefing produced 24 Nov 2026, 3:00 PM NZDT

The Israeli military completed a ground operation in central Gaza, advancing more than 1.2km beyond the Yellow Line to dismantle a tunnel, according to the IDF. Residents near Nuseirat and Bureij refugee camps were ordered to evacuate, with an estimated 6,000 people fleeing their homes. Hamas accused Israel of violating the October 2025 ceasefire, while the IDF stated the operation targeted an immediate threat to its troops.

Why it matters

The incursion marks the first publicly announced Israeli ground operation beyond the Yellow Line since the ceasefire began, raising concerns about the stability of the truce and the ongoing displacement of Gaza's population.

Daily News

Business · Technology · AI · Economy

Anthropic raises $81bn in record-breaking stock market debut

Global · United States · Major · Updated

Briefing produced 24 Nov 2026, 3:00 PM NZDT

Anthropic raised a record $81.3 billion in its Nasdaq IPO debut, valuing the AI company at approximately $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis. The company's shares closed 17% higher at $97.17 on their first day of trading, after briefly surpassing a $2 trillion market valuation.

Why it matters

As the first purely AI-focused firm to publicly sell shares, Anthropic's debut serves as a crucial test for investor confidence in the fast-growing AI sector. The listing provides direct public market exposure to a frontier AI developer while highlighting ongoing concerns about the industry's financial sustainability and massive infrastructure costs.

Environment · Technology · Business

Meta reconsiders 2030 net-zero goal amid record emissions from AI data centers

Global · Notable · Updated

Briefing produced 24 Nov 2026, 3:00 PM NZDT

Meta is re-evaluating its 2030 net-zero emissions goal and interim milestones in its 2026 sustainability report, citing AI infrastructure demand that grew faster than projected. The company reported a nearly 40% increase in total carbon emissions to over 21.7 million metric tonnes in 2025, the highest year-over-year percentage increase among major US tech giants.

Why it matters

Meta's public acknowledgment of re-evaluating its 2030 target distinguishes it from Amazon, Google, and Microsoft, which have maintained their original sustainability goals despite similar challenges in balancing emissions with hyperscale data center buildouts.

Europe ready for talks with Russia on ending war in Ukraine, leaders say

Ukraine · Russia · Europe · Major · Previously featured

Briefing produced 24 Nov 2026, 3:00 PM NZDT

European leaders at a Berlin summit declared readiness for negotiations with Russia to end the war in Ukraine, with UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham stating Europe has a united position. US envoy Jared Kushner reported that Moscow is comfortable with Ukraine receiving Article Five-style security guarantees, though European leaders remained skeptical of Russian intentions. Meanwhile, Russian drones attacked Kyiv, killing one person and damaging historic buildings.

Why it matters

The potential inclusion of Europe in peace talks and the prospect of security guarantees for Ukraine represent significant shifts in the diplomatic landscape, though Russia continues to demand Ukrainian sovereign territory and intensify attacks on civilian infrastructure.

Tech stock sell-off drags markets down as Anthropic shares slide

Global · Major · Previously featured

Briefing produced 24 Nov 2026, 3:00 PM NZDT

US stock markets fell sharply on Friday, with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones entering correction territory, as a tech sell-off dragged indices down. Anthropic shares dropped 8.5% to near their IPO price, reversing half of their first-day gains, while Nvidia fell 13.7% amid unconfirmed reports of an SEC investigation. Russia targets Kyiv crossings days after Ukraine hits Crimean Bridge

Ukraine · Russia · Poland · Major · Catch up

Briefing produced 24 Nov 2026, 3:00 PM NZDT

Misunderstanding these legal thresholds can lead to complicated and expensive break-ups, as individuals may fail to protect assets or realize that de facto claims can arise even without shared housing or bank accounts.

When threatening to leave unlocks a better deal

NZ · Useful · New

Briefing produced 24 Nov 2026, 3:00 PM NZDT

New Zealand customers reported receiving significant discounts, such as 50% off antivirus or magazine subscriptions, only after threatening to cancel. Marketing experts describe this as "tactical termination," noting that while retention discounts are financially rational for businesses, they can undermine customer trust and teach consumers to threaten cancellation to secure fair prices.

Why it matters

Experts warn that this practice creates a "loyalty tax" where existing customers pay more than new ones, potentially leading to long-term brand damage and a shift toward transactional rather than relationship-based consumer interactions.

NASA’s new Moon plan is taking shape, but some big questions remain

Global · Notable · Updated

Briefing produced 23 Nov 2026, 3:00 AM NZDT

NASA has restructured the Artemis program to convert Artemis III into a low-Earth orbit test mission for 2027, delaying the first crewed lunar landing to Artemis IV before the end of 2028. This change removes the previous 90-day lunar orbit loiter requirement, replacing it with an Earth orbit rendezvous to simplify lander operations for SpaceX and Blue Origin.

Why it matters

The architectural shift imposes significant technical challenges on the Orion spacecraft, which was not originally designed for extended low-Earth orbit stays or the reversed flying posture required for Starship docking. These changes create a compressed schedule for integration work and introduce new risks regarding orbital debris and thermal management that must be addressed before the 2027 launch.
